decision_maker: Director of Public Health, Customer and Community Wellbeing (DPH)
content:
Following consideration of consultation
responses and the latest evidence of anti-social behaviour (ASB) in
the alleyway between Chapel Street and Main Street, Egremont, it
has been decided to make a Public Spaces Protection Order (PSPO)
under sections 59, 61, 64 and 72 of the Anti-Social Behaviour,
Crime and Policing Act 2014.(the Act)
 
The Order will :
• Restrict the public right of way
through the alleyway, enforced by installation gates at both
ends.
• Provide exemptions for residents,
emergency services, statutory undertakers, and authorised Council
officers.
• Ensure alternative pedestrian access
via Chapel Street.
• Remain in effect for a period of three
years, subject to review and potential extension.
 
The Council will publish the Order, erect
appropriate signage, and implement enforcement arrangements in
accordance with statutory requirements

The decision to make the PSPO is based on the
following legal, evidential, and practical reasons:
 
Legal compliance
• Section 59 of the 2014 Act requires
that:
o Activities have,
or are likely to have, a detrimental effect on the quality of life
of those in the locality.
o The effect is persistent, continuing, and
unreasonable. o Restrictions are justified to prevent
recurrence.
• Section 61 allows restrictions on
public rights of way.
• Section 64 allows installation of gates
to enforce these restrictions.
• Section 72 requires consultation and
publicity, which has been completed. Evidential basis
• The evidence shows a pattern of
persistent, continuing behaviour affecting residents’ quality
of life.
Proportionality and necessity
• Gating the alleyway is a proportionate
response given the severity and persistence of the ASB.
• Alternative interventions (e.g.,
monitoring by the Local Focus Hub) will not resolve the problem
following the most recent evidence of ASB on the alleyway.
• Exemptions ensure that residents,
emergency services, and statutory undertakers retain reasonable
access, minimising intrusion.
Community support and consultation
• Consultation with residents, statutory
bodies, and emergency services indicates sufficient support for
gating. Risk management
• Without intervention, ASB may escalate,
causing further harm, distress, and property damage.
• Making the PSPO reduces the risk of
future complaints and supports a safer local environment.

 
• Do nothing – rejected, as
evidence now shows persistent ASB affecting residents.
• Alternative interventions only –
rejected. The previous Non-Key Officer Decision Report referred the
matter to the Local Focus Hub for monitoring and review. However,
since that report further evidence as indicated in this report, has
come to light to support the making of the PSPO.
• Proceed with making the PSPO –
selected option, as it is necessary, proportionate, and lawful
under the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014
topline: The Director of Public Health has decided to implement a Public Spaces Protection Order in an alleyway in Egremont to address persistent anti-social behaviour.

content:
That the Assistant Director authorises the
Chief Legal Officer to make an order under Section 257 of the Town
and Country Planning Act 1990
 
to stop up public footpath no 120007 in the
parish of Kingmoor as shown A-B on the attached order plan and
 
to divert public footpath no 120008 in the
parish of Kingmoor as shown B-C to a new route D-E-F-G-H-I-J-C as
shown on the attached order plan
 
and in the event no objections are made to the
order, that the Chief Legal Officer be authorised to confirm the
order

Public Footpath Nos 120007 and 120008 follow
alignments through the development area and would be impacted by
the proposed development. 
 
Local Plan Policy G15 states that new
development will be expected to ensure that all public rights of
way are retained and proposals that would affect existing rights of
way will not be permitted unless an alternative route is available,
or can be made available, which is safe, attractive, is well
integrated with the existing network and is not significantly
longer than the original routes.
 
The proposed new route starts on the Carlisle
Northern Development Route (CNDR) at the business park’s
southern entrance and follows the existing footway before crossing
Dukes Drive via a provided crossing point with associated dropped
kerbs and tactile surfacing.  It then
continues along the wide footway of the spine road a short distance
before crossing over, again via another crossing point with dropped
kerbs and tactile surfacing. 
 
From there, the proposed path parallels the
course of Cargo Beck along a 2-metre wide, newly constructed,
asphalt surfaced path through a newly landscaped, traffic-free,
green space to meet the unaffected section of footpath at point
C.
 
The proposed stopping up and diversion is
necessary to enable development to be carried out.
 
As the development is to obstruct the legal
alignment of the footpaths then the formal stopping up and
diversion must be brought into effect before the development work
is commenced.
 

The options considered are:-
 
a.        Not to make
the Order, or
b.        To make the
Order as requested.
 
If the Order is not made then the existing
public footpaths will be obstructed for the most part by the
development.  In doing so the council
will fall foul of its legal duty under section 130 of the Highways
Act 1980 to “assert and protect the rights of the public to
the use and enjoyment of any highway for which they are the highway
authority”.
 
If the Order is made as requested, the
footpaths will be diverted to a new route within the development to
preserve historic highway links.
 
The Council has discretion as to whether or
not to make an order, but such discretion must be exercised
reasonably. Taking into account the
options available to the Council, the option to not make the Order
has been rejected and the recommendation to make the Order is
proposed.
topline: The Assistant Director of Thriving Places has decided to authorise the stopping up and diversion of public footpaths in Kingmoor for development purposes.

content:
A request has been received for
the Council to waive the repayment on a DFG Repayment under the
Housing Renewal Assistance Policy 2021 CL-004349.
. The
Housing Renewal Assistance policy document, lays out the
reasons for using discretion to waive the payment.
 
Taking into
account all the available information,
a decision has been taken to agree to waive the
repayment of £4152.56
 

The decision has been made to waive the
requirement to repay the DFG on grounds that the disposal of the
property is being made for reasons of the recipient’s
physical health and well-being.

Alternative options considered,
 
1) Require the family to make a repayment to
the Council upon the sale of the property and not use the
discretion to waive the repayment laid out within the policy
framework.
 
2) Require repayments to be made through
debtors over a period of up to 5 years. This would include
additional administration costs and interest charges during the
repayment period.

Proposal: Hybrid
planning submission compromising full application for
industrial/workshop/trade counter & logistics units, together
with site accesses, service roads, development platforms, drainage
lagoons & associated service infrastructure & landscaping;
Outline application for further industrial & logistics units
& roadside services within use classes and Sui Generis to
include roadside facilities such as EV charging facility/petrol
filling station/restaurant/drive thru restaurant & public
house.
 
The Planning Officer submitted a report which
had been subject to a site visit on Monday 13 October 2025.
 
Slides were displayed on screen showing: wider
location plan, context location plan, location plan, site plan,
parameters plan, plot 3000 (full application), indicative
masterplan, junction 44, site access off A7, indicative view of the
site entrance, indicative view across plot 3000, indicative view
between plots 3000 & 3200, plots 3000 & 4000 view towards
Harker Lodge, indicative view from Harker Lodge, indicative view
from Harker Lodge, indicative view across M6, indicative aerial
view and photographs of the site. An explanation of which was
provided for the benefit of Members.
 
The Planning Officer drew Members attention to
the update report which contained a further objection, revised
wording for the recommendation and four new conditions to be
included. A verbal update was provided that the amended wording for
the cycleway contribution had been amended further since the update
report had been published to £49,300 towards the provision of
cycleways and associated works from junction 44 into Carlisle,
payable prior to commencement of development.
 
The Planning Officer recommended that the
application is approved subject to the conditions including the
four additional conditions, delegated authority be given to the
Service Manager for Development and Implementation to add to and/or
make any amendments to the conditions as considered appropriate,
and to agree the final terms and conditions of the S106 agreement,
which, as amended, are proposed as:
 

·        
£49,300 towards the provision of cycleways and associated
works from junction 44 into Carlisle, payable prior to commencement
of development;

·        
£94,409.09 towards the completion of the signalisation of the
Parkhouse Roundabout, payable prior to commencement of
development;

·        
£11,880 to be apportioned on a per-unit basis towards Travel
Plan Monitoring, payable prior to the occupation of each relevant
unit;

·        
£6,500 to fund a Traffic Regulation Order (TRO) for the speed
limit change on the A7, payable prior to commencement of
development.
 
The Senior Lawyer advised Members that the
Council owned a parcel of land within the red line boundary of the
application site, however this did not affect the application and
was not a material consideration, Members were advised for
transparency purposes.
 
 
 
Representation:
 
Two objectors spoke in objection to the
application.
 
The Parish Councillor spoke in objection to
the application.
 
The Ward Councillor spoke in objection to the
application.
 
The Agent spoke in support of the
application.
 
In response to the objections raised that
consultations had not taken place, the Planning Officer advised
Members that consultation had taken place at the onset of the
application and that re-consultation would only be carried out if
there had been significant changes to the application.
 
A Member asked for an adjournment to read the
update report, the Chair of the Committee reminded Members that
they had been sent the update report however would adjourn the
meeting for 5 minutes to ensure Members were satisfied with the
information submitted within the report.
 
The Planning
Committee adjourned at 11.17am and reconvened at 11.23am
 
A Member asked for clarification of the term
Sui Generis within the proposal, in response the Planning Officer
clarified that Sui Generis is a broad term for something that did
not fit within the defined use classes.
 
A discussion took place in regard to the
de-trunking of the A69 at Warwick Bridge and a Member queried if
this had been taken into account by National Highways in so far as
this would increase traffic, when National Highways responded to
the application. The members informed the committee that they were
aware that the de-trunking had been marked as a priority by
National Highways.
 
The Planning Officer confirmed that
discussions had taken place with National Highways where the
Carlisle Southern Link Road had been discussed, so they had an
awareness of this.
 
The Senior Lawyer clarified that as stated,
discussions had taken place with National Highways and that they
were aware of the priority of de-trunking of the A69, as confirmed
by Members, and that National Highways were also aware of the
southern link road. However, Members were reminded that due to the
de-trunking of the A69 not having been formalised hypothetical
scenarios and impact should not be taken into account when reaching
the decision of the application in front of them. Members should
only take into account what is before them.
 
Members asked for reassurance that J44 would
not be severely impacted with the increase in traffic, however they
could see the economic benefits of the application.
 
Councillor Markley
left the meeting
 
In response the Planning Officer clarified
that National Highways had confirmed that the transport impacts had
been appropriately addressed.
 
Following further consideration of the
application a Member moved to accept the Officer’s
recommendation. This was seconded.
 
A vote was taken:
7 voted in favour, 1 against, 0
abstentions
 
 
RESOLVED – That the application
be approved subject to the conditions set out below, with delegated
authority be given to the Service Manager for Development and
Implementation to add to and/or make any amendments to the
conditions as considered appropriate, and to agree the final terms
and conditions of the S106 agreement which detailed above are
proposed as:
 

·        
£49,300 towards the provision of cycleways and associated
works from junction 44 into Carlisle, payable prior to commencement
of development;

·        
£94,409.09 towards the completion of the signalisation of the
Parkhouse Roundabout, payable prior to commencement of
development;

·        
£11,880 to be apportioned on a per-unit basis towards Travel
Plan Monitoring, payable prior to the occupation of each relevant
unit;

·        
£6,500 to fund a Traffic Regulation Order (TRO) for the speed
limit change on the A7, payable prior to commencement of
development.
 
Conditions
 




 


 
Conditions 1 to 22
relate specifically to the full planning permission, which
comprises the erection of industrial, workshop, trade counter, and
logistics units (Use Classes B2, B8, and E(g)) on Plot 3000,
together with site accesses, service roads, footways and cycle
routes, development platforms, drainage lagoons, associated service
infrastructure, and landscaping.

The part of the development hereby granted
full permission (i.e. Plot 3000) shall be begun not later than the
expiration of 3 years beginning with the date of the grant of this
permission.
 
Reason: In accordance with the
provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990
(as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase
Act 2004).

(dwg no. 17045-FSA-30-XX-DR-A-7201 Rev

Reason: To define the permission.
 




3.


Prior to the occupation of the first unit
within Plot 3000 hereby permitted, the cycleway, access roundabout,
and all ancillary works connecting the site to Junction 44 shall be
completed. Details of these works shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
 
Reason: To ensure a minimum standard of
construction in the interests of highway safety, and to support
Local Transport Plan Policies LD5, LD7, and LD8.
 




4.


Highways details associated with any unit /
sub-unit of the development within Plot 3000 hereby approved by the
Full Planning Permission must be submitted to and approved in
writing by the local planning authority prior to any highway works
for that unit / sub-unit being commenced. These details shall
include the carriageway, footways, footpaths, cycleways etc and
shall be designed, constructed, drained and lit to a standard
suitable for adoption and in this respect further details,
including longitudinal/cross sections, shall be submitted to the
local planning authority for approval before highway works within
any unit / sub-unit commence. No highway works shall be commenced
until a full specification has been approved in writing by the
local planning authority. These details shall be in accordance with
the standards laid down in the current Cumbria Design Guide. Any
works so approved including the carriageway, footways, footpaths
and cycleways shall be constructed in strict accordance with the
approved details and completed prior to the relevant unit /sub-unit
being brought into use.
 
Reason: To ensure a minimum standard of
construction in the interests of highway safety, and to support
Local Transport Plan Policies LD5, LD7, and LD8.
 




5.


The use of the development shall not commence
until the access and internal access roads serving the completed
unit have been constructed in accordance with the approved details
and as shown on the Parameters Plan (dwg no. 17045-FSA-00-XX-DR-A-0203 Rev P08, received
22 Sept 2025).
 
Reason: To support Local Transport Plan
Policies LD5, LD7, and LD8.
 




6.


Prior to the commencement of construction of
any unit, details of the access arrangements and internal layout to
accommodate bus access into the site shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved
arrangements shall be implemented and shall be retained thereafter
for the lifetime of the development.
 
Reason: To ensure a minimum standard of
access provision when the development is brought into use. To
support Local Transport Plan Policies: LD5, LD7
 




7.


The use shall not be commenced until the
access and parking requirements have been constructed in accordance
with the approved proposed site plan for plot 3000 (dwg no. 17045-FSA-30-XX-DR-A-0200 Rev P08, received
22nd September 2025). Any such access and or parking provision
shall be retained and be capable of use when the development is
completed and shall not be removed or altered without the prior
consent of the Local Planning Authority.
 
Reason: In the interests of highway
safety, and to support Local Transport Plan Policies LD5, LD7, and
LD8.




8.


Prior to the occupation of any unit or
sub-unit within Plot 3000 hereby approved by the Full Planning
Permission, the Travel Plan prepared by Tetra Tech (dated November
2022), or any subsequent updated version approved in writing by the
local planning authority, shall be implemented in full. The use of
the relevant unit shall thereafter be carried out in full
accordance with the approved Travel Plan, unless otherwise agreed
in writing by the local planning authority.
 
Reason: In the interests of highway
safety, and to support Local Transport Plan Policies LD5, LD7, and
LD8.
 




9.


No unit / sub-unit within Plot 3000 hereby
approved by the Full Planning Permission shall commence until a
Construction Traffic Management Plan (CTMP) has been submitted to
and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The CTMP
shall include details of:


·        
details of proposed crossings of the highway verge;

·        
retained areas for vehicle parking, manoeuvring, loading and
unloading for their specific purpose during the development;

·        
cleaning of site entrances and the adjacent public highway;

·        
details of proposed wheel washing facilities;

·        
the sheeting of all HGVs taking spoil to/from the site to prevent
spillage or deposit of any materials on the highway;

·        
construction vehicle routing;

·        
the management of junctions to and crossings of the public highway
and other public rights of way/footway;

·        
details of any proposed temporary access points if any is to be
used (vehicular / pedestrian)

·        
surface water management details during the construction phase
 
The agreed scheme shall be implemented upon
commencement of development on the relevant plot / sub-plot and
shall not be varied without prior written agreement of the local
planning authority.
 
Reason: To ensure the undertaking of
the development does not adversely impact upon the fabric or
operation of the local highway network and in the interests of
highway and pedestrian safety.
 




10.


Where relevant, no unit or sub-unit within
Plot 3000 hereby approved by the Full Planning Permission shall
commence until full details of the surface water drainage system
and a foul water drainage system (incorporating SUDS features where
practicable) and a maintenance schedule (identifying the
responsible parties) have been submitted to and approved in writing
by the local planning authority. The drainage schemes shall
include:
 

·        
An investigation of the hierarchy of drainage options in the
Planning Practice Guidance (or any subsequent amendment thereof).
This investigation shall include evidence of an assessment of
ground conditions and the potential for infiltration of surface
water in accordance with BRE365.

·        
A restricted rate of discharge of surface water agreed with the
local planning authority (if it is agreed that infiltration is
discounted by the investigations).

·        
Level of the proposed drainage system including proposed ground and
finished floor levels in AOD.

·        
Incorporate mitigation measures to manage the risk of sewer
surcharge where applicable.

·        
Full details of the permanent solution for foul.
Foul and surface water shall drain on separate
systems. The approved schemes shall be in accordance with the
Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems
(March 2015) or any subsequent replacement national standards. The
approved drainage works for a plot / sub-plot shall be completed
prior to the occupation of the relevant plot / sub-plot and shall
thereafter be maintained in accordance with the approved
details.
 
Reason: To promote sustainable
development, secure proper drainage and to manage the risk of
flooding and pollution. To ensure the surface water system
continues to function as designed and that flood risk is not
increased within the site or elsewhere.
 




11.


No unit or sub-unit within Plot 3000 hereby
approved by the Full Planning Permission shall commence until a
Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) for that plot /
sub-plot has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local
planning authority. The approved CEMP shall be implemented upon
commencement of development within the relevant plot / sub-plot and
shall not be varied without prior written agreement of the local
planning authority. The CEMP shall include and address the
following matters (where appropriate):
 
i) Provision of appropriate protective
barriers / boundary hoarding and lighting.
ii) Dust management and details of the
proposed means of dust suppression.
iii) Details of deliveries times to the site
during the construction phase.
iv) The construction hours of working.
v) Noise management measures.
vi) Programme of works (including measures for
traffic management and operating hours).
vii) Loading and unloading of plant and
materials.
viii) Piling techniques.
ix) Location and nature of compounds and
storage areas (including maximum storage heights) and factors to
prevent wind-whipping.
x) Waste storage and removal and litter
management.
xi) Temporary buildings and boundary
treatments.
xii) Details of checks of vehicles and other
plant for leaks.
xiii) Static plant to be placed on drip
trays.
xiv) Preparation of cement and other
construction materials.
xv) Waste minimisation and management
measures.
xvi) Bio-security measures to prevent the
introduction of disease and invasive Species.
xvii) Measures to prevent pollution including
the management of site drainage such as the use of silt traps
during construction.
xviii) The checking and testing of imported
fill material where required to ensure suitability for use and
prevent the spread of invasive species.
xix) Noise and vibration management (to
include arrangements for monitoring, and specifically for any
concrete breaking and any piling).
xx) There shall be no burning of materials on
the site.
xxi) Any external lighting associated with the
development during any ground works/construction for the purposes
of security and site safety shall prevent upward and outward light
radiation.
xxii) Protocols for contact and consultation
with local people and other matters to be agreed with the local
planning authority.
xxiii) Wheel washing.
xxiv) Vibration management.
xxv) Vermin control.
xxvi) Vehicle control within the site and
localised traffic management.
 
The agreed scheme shall be implemented upon
commencement of the relevant plot / sub-plot and shall not be
varied without prior written agreement of the local planning
authority.
 
Reason: To ensure that appropriate
environmental management measures are in place during the
construction phase in the interests of protecting residential
amenity, local air quality, biodiversity, and the surrounding
environment, in accordance with Policies SP6 and CM5 of the
Carlisle District Local Plan and the aims of the National Planning
Policy Framework.
 




12.


Prior to the commencement of any demolition
work of the Grearshill Farm buildings,
a Level 3 Historic Building Record of the buildings to be
demolished shall be undertaken in accordance with Historic
England's guidance 'Understanding Historic Buildings: A Guide to
Good Recording Practice' (or any subsequent replacement guidance).
The completed record shall be submitted to and approved in writing
by the local planning authority and deposited with the relevant
Historic Environment Record prior to the commencement of the
relevant demolition works.
 
Reason: To ensure that a proper record
is made of any historic buildings affected by the development, in
accordance with the guidance set out in the National Planning
Policy Framework and Historic England’s ‘Understanding
Historic Buildings: A Guide to Good Recording Practice’.
 




13.


No development of any unit or sub-unit within
Plot 3000 hereby approved by the Full Planning Permission shall
commence until a programme of archaeological work has been secured
and implemented in accordance with a written scheme of
investigation that has been submitted to and approved in writing by
the local planning authority. This written scheme will include the
following components:
i) An archaeological evaluation;
ii) An archaeological recording programme the
scope of which will be dependant upon
the results of the evaluation;
iii) If significant archaeological remains are
identified during the programme of archaeological work, the
following shall be undertaken within one year of the completion of
that programme on site, or within such other timescale as may be
agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority:
 

A post-excavation assessment and
analysis;
Preparation of a site archive
suitable for deposition at a location approved by the Local
Planning Authority;
Completion of an archive report;
and
Submission of the findings for
publication in an appropriate academic or professional
journal.

 
Reason: To afford reasonable
opportunity for an examination to be made to determine the
existence of any remains of archaeological interest within the site
and for the preservation, examination or recording of such remains,
in accordance with Policy HE2 of the Carlisle District Local Plan
2015-2030.
 




14.


Prior to the commencement of the use of any
unit within Plot 3000 hereby approved by the Full Planning
Permission, details of the proposed Acoustic Fencing and an
Operational Noise Management Plan shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved
Acoustic Fencing shall be fully installed prior to the commencement
of the use of the relevant unit and shall be retained and
maintained thereafter. The use of the unit shall thereafter be
carried out in full accordance with the approved Operational Noise
Management Plan for the lifetime of the relevant unit.
 
Reason: To safeguard the amenity of
nearby sensitive receptors from noise associated with the operation
of the development, in accordance with national and Policy CM5 of
the Carlisle District Local Plan 2015-2030 relating to
environmental protection and residential amenity.
 




15.


Prior to the commencement of any unit or
sub-unit within Plot 3000, a landscaping scheme which includes
details of retained habitats of the development authorised by the
Full Planning Permission shall be implemented in strict accordance
with a detailed proposal that has first been submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning authority.  The scheme shall include details of the
following:
 
i) New areas of trees and shrubs to be planted
including planting densities.
ii) New groups and individual specimen trees
and shrubs to be planted.
iii) Specification / age / heights of trees
and shrubs to be planted.
iv) Existing trees and shrubs to be retained
or removed.
v) Any tree surgery / management works
proposed in relation to retained trees and shrubs.
vi) Any remodelling of ground to facilitate
the planting.
vii) Timing of the landscaping in terms of the
phasing of the development.
viii) Protection, maintenance and aftercare
measures.
ix) A woodland buffer zone around any residential properties
located close to or within the site, where applicable, to provide
visual screening and ecological enhancement.
 
Reason: To ensure the development
delivers a high-quality landscape setting, retains and enhances
existing habitats, and contributes positively to biodiversity,
visual amenity, and the character of the area, in accordance with
Policies SP6, GI1 and GI3 of the Carlisle District Local Plan
2015-2030.
 




16.


All planting, seeding, or turfing comprised in
the approved details of landscaping and retained habitats shall be
carried out within the timeframe set out in the landscaping scheme
approved by the local planning authority pursuant to Condition 15
and shall be maintained thereafter in accordance with that scheme.
Any trees or plants which, within a period of 5 years from the
completion of the unit/sub-unit within Plot 3000 hereby approved by
the Full Planning Permission, die, are removed, or become seriously
damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season
with others of similar size and species, unless otherwise agreed in
writing by the local planning authority.
 
Reason: To ensure the timely
implementation and long-term maintenance of landscaping and habitat
features, in the interests of visual amenity, biodiversity
enhancement, and the character of the area, in accordance with
Policies GI3 and GI6 of the Carlisle District Local Plan
2015–2030.
 




17.


No development shall commence until a detailed
Habitat Creation and Management Strategy has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The
Strategy will show how a biodiversity net gain has been
achieved, demonstrated with a Biodiversity Metric, and shall
include:


Details of all habitat creation,
enhancement, and management measures (including native tree, shrub,
and wildflower planting, hedgerow creation, and provision of
ditches, where necessary for that phase);

·        
A timetable for implementation;
·        
Details of ongoing management and monitoring for a minimum period
of 30 years;
·        
Provisions for review and remedial measures if targets are not
met.

The development shall be carried out in
accordance with the approved Strategy.
 
If the Biodiversity Metric demonstrates that a
net gain cannot be achieved on-site, no development (excluding
demolition, site clearance, or groundworks) shall commence until a
scheme of off-site biodiversity compensation has been submitted to
and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme
shall include details of the location, extent, and management of
off-site habitat creation, and a timetable for delivery. The scheme
shall be implemented as approved.
 
Reason: To secure the creation,
enhancement, and long-term management of ecological features and
habitats within the development, ensuring biodiversity net gain and
compliance with Policies GI3 and GI6 of the Carlisle District Local
Plan 2015–2030, and the objectives of the National Planning
Policy Framework.
 




18.


Prior to development commencing on site,
updated protected species survey are required and where necessary,
appropriate protected species mitigation licences must be obtained.
The results of the protected species surveys and proof of a licence
(if one is required) must be submitted to and approved in writing

In the event that contamination is found at
any time when carrying out the approved development that was not
previously identified it must be reported in writing immediately to
the Local Planning Authority. An investigation and risk assessment
must be undertaken and where remediation is necessary a remediation
scheme must be prepared, which is subject to the approval in
writing of the Local Planning Authority. Site investigations should
follow the guidance in BS10175:2011 (or updated version)
“Investigation of Potentially Contaminated Sites.- Code of
Practice.”
 
Following completion of measures identified in
the approved remediation scheme a verification report must be
prepared, which is subject to the approval in writing of the Local
Planning Authority.
 
Reason: To ensure that risks from land
contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land
are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, property
and ecological systems, and to ensure that the development can be
carried out safely without unacceptable risks to workers,
neighbours and other offsite receptors in accordance with Policy
CM5 of the Carlisle District Local Plan 2015-2030.
 




49.      Prior to the occupation of any
unit within Plot 4000 (Sub-plots 4100 and 4200), as shown on the
Parameters Plan (Drawing No. 17045-FSA-00-XX-DR-A-0203 Rev P08,
received 9 November 2022), where the proposed use falls within a
public house, restaurant, or drive-thru restaurant use, a detailed
odour assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by
the Local Planning Authority. The assessment shall include any
necessary mitigation measures to minimise odour impacts on nearby
sensitive receptors. The approved measures shall be implemented in
full prior to occupation and retained thereafter.
 
Reason: To
minimise odour impacts on neighbouring residential properties and
ensure an acceptable standard of amenity, in accordance with Policy
CM5 of the Carlisle District Local Plan 2015-2030.
 
50.      Within six months of any units
within Plot 4000 (Sub-plots 4100 and 4200), as shown on the
Parameters Plan (Drawing No. 17045-FSA-00-XX-DR-A-0203 Rev P08,
received 9 November 2022), being brought into first use, a
Servicing Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by
the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall include details of
the provision of external litter bins, including their
specifications and planned emptying frequencies. The development
shall thereafter be operated in accordance with the approved
details.
 
Reason: To
ensure that adequate means of litter management is provided in
accordance with policy IP5 and SP6 of the Carlisle District Local
Plan 2015-2030. To further safeguard the amenity of surrounding
properties, it is proposed to require the submission of lighting
details for Plots 1000, 2000, and 4000, and to restrict
construction hours through the imposition of additional planning
conditions.
 
51.        Prior to
installation of any external lighting within Plots 1000, 2000, and
4000, details of the proposed external lighting (inclusive of the
design, locations and luminance levels) shall be submitted to the
local planning authority for approval in writing. The development
shall only be carried out in accordance with the approved
details.
 
Reason: To
safeguard the living conditions of the neighbouring residents and
to ensure the objectives of Policies CM5 and SP6 of the Carlisle
District Local Plan 2015-2030 are met.
 
52.      No work associated with the
construction of the development hereby approved shall be carried
out before 07.30 hours on weekdays and Saturdays nor after 1800
hours on weekdays and 1300 hours on Saturdays (nor at any times on
Sundays or statutory holidays).
 
Reason: To
prevent disturbance to nearby occupants in accordance with Policy
CM5 of the Carlisle District Local Plan 2015-2030.

Proposal: Removal of
existing wind turbine and erection of replacement wind turbine, up
to 76m blade tip height, with associated development.
 
The Head of Planning and Place submitted a
report which had been subject to a site visit on Monday 13 October
2025.
 
Slides were displayed on screen showing:
Location context plan, site location plan, typical elevation plan,
proposed layout plan, zone of theoretical influence –
operational & proposed turbines (25km), visualisation –
viewpoint from Bigrigg, visualisation – viewpoint from St
Bees, visualisation – viewpoint from Cleator Moor,
visualisation – viewpoint from the Laurels, Egremont,
visualisation – Stanley View, Whitehaven, visualisation
– viewpoint from Costal Path, St Bees, visualisation –
viewpoint from Blake Fell, LDNP, Coronation Terrace & adjacent
properties, Coronation Terrace – existing & proposed, Low
Walton – existing & proposed, proposed access
arrangements, energy generation and photographs of the site. An
explanation of which was provided for the benefit of Members.
 
The Head of Planning and Place recommended
that the application be approved subject to the conditions with the
Service manager for Development and Implementation being given
delegated authority to add to and/or make any amendments to the
conditions as considered appropriate.
 
The Head of Planning and Place also advised
Members that condition 16 would be deleted, it was no longer
necessary to include this condition as the BNG proposed shall be
secured by the deemed condition pursuant to Paragraph 13 Schedule
7A Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
 
Representation:
 
The Parish Councillor spoke in objection to
the application.
 
The Agent spoke in support of the
application.
 
A Member questioned if the turbines could be
programmed to stop shadow flicker, in response the Agent advised
that they could slow down or cease the turbine at certain times of
the year. The Member asked the Officer if they could review it in
future and intervene if a problem occurred, The Head of Planning
and Place advised referred to the proposed condition 10 and advised
Members that Officer’s could
intervene if it became a problem.
 
Following consideration of the application a
Member moved to accept the officer’s recommendation. This was
seconded.
 
A vote was taken:
8 voted in favour, 0 against, 0
abstentions.
 
RESOLVED – That the application
be approved subject to the conditions set out below with delegated
authority given to the Service Manager for Development and
Implementation to add to and/or make any amendments to the
conditions as considered appropriate.
 
 
Conditions
 

The development hereby permitted
shall begin not later than three years from the date of this
decision.

 
Reason: To
comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country
Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and
Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.
 

The development hereby permitted
shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved
plans and documents:



Application Form
Site Location Plan, drawing number
3369-090-LP-001
Site Plan, drawing number
3369-090-SP-002
Block Plan – Access, drawing
number 3369-090-OA-005
Access Plan, drawing number
3369-090-TA-004
Turbine Site Area, drawing number
3369-090-TSA-006
Highfield Farm Wind Turbine
Repowering - Landscape and Visual Appraisal – Report Ref.
3369-09-LVA-01
Highfield Farm Wind Turbine
Repowering on behalf of Axis PED Preliminary Ecological Appraisal
– Report Ref. AxisL-043-8710
Highfield Farm Wind Turbine
Repowering Planning Statement Report Ref. 3369-09-PS-01
Highfield Farm Wind Turbine
Repowering Planning Statement Addendum Ref. 3369-09-PSA-03


 
Reason: For
the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.
 
Duration of the
Planning Permission
 

This planning permission is for a
period not exceeding 25 (twenty five) years from the date that
electricity from the development is first connected into the
National Grid.

The Local Planning
Authority shall be notified in writing of the date of the
commissioning of the wind turbine no later than one calendar month
after date of commissioning.
 
Reason: To
ensure that possible dereliction and unsightliness is avoided in
accordance with Policy DS4 and Policy N6 of the Copeland Local Plan
2021-2039.
 
Wind Turbine
Generator Specifications
 

The maximum height of the wind
turbine generator hereby permitted shall not exceed 76 metres above
ground level when a blade is in the vertical position.

 
Reason: For
the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of amenity and visual
impact in accordance with Policies DS4 and N6 of the Copeland Local
Plan 2021-2039.
 

No logos, advertisements, lettering,
lights or other information (other than that required for health
and safety purposes or required for legal reasons including
aviation safety) shall be displayed on the wind turbine generator
hereby approved.

 
Reason: For
the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of amenity and visual
impact in accordance with Policies DS4 and N6 of the Copeland Local
Plan 2021-2039.
 

No development shall commence until
detailed plans, specifications and drawings of the wind turbine
generator to be installed shall be submitted to and agreed in
writing by the Local Planning Authority.

 
Reason: For
the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of amenity and visual
impact in accordance with Policies DS4 and N6 of the Copeland Local
Plan 2021-2039.
 
Micro-siting
 

The wind turbine generator and site
access hereby approved shall be constructed in the locations shown
on:

Site Plan - Drawing
No. 3369-091-SP-002 Version A
Block Plan –
Turbine Site – Drawing No. 3369-091-TSA-006 Version A
Access Plan –
Drawing No. 3369-091-TA-004 Version A
The wind turbine
generator and site access may be adjusted by micro-siting within
the Application Site.
Micro-siting is
subject to the following restrictions:

The wind turbine generator shall be moved no more than 10m from the
approved position.

The height of foundation of the wind turbine generator shall not be
increased from the approved position.

The site access shall be moved no more than 1m from the approved
position.
 
Reason: For
the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of amenity and visual
impact in accordance with Policies DS4 and N6 of the Copeland Local
Plan 2021-2039.
 
Operational
Limitations
 

The noise emissions from the wind
turbine shall not exceed:

(i)           
a level of 35 dB LA90 (10 minutes) during the daytime (07.00
– 23.00 hours) and 43 dB LA90 (10 minutes) during the night
time (23.00 – 07.00 hours) or ETSU derived limits of
background noise level plus 5 dB (whichever is greater) at the
curtilage of any dwelling lawfully existing at the time of this
consent for all wind speeds up to 10 m/s at 10 m height; and
(ii) For properties
with a valid financial interest, the noise limit shall not exceed a
level of 45 dB LA90 (10 minutes) or ETSU derived limit of
background noise level plus 5 dB (whichever is greater) for all
wind speeds up to 10 m/s at 10 m height shall apply.
 
Reason: In
order to safeguard the amenities of adjoining residential occupiers
in accordance with Policy DS4 of the Copeland Local Plan 2021-2039.
Site Specific Construction Environmental Management Plan
 

Within 28 days from the receipt of a
written request from the Local Planning Authority, following a
noise complaint to it, the wind turbine generator operator shall,
at the wind turbine operators expense, employ an independent
consultant approved by the Local Planning Authority to assess the
level of noise emissions from the wind turbine at the
complainant’s property following the procedures described in
‘The Assessment and Rating of Noise from Wind Farms,
ETSU-R-97’. Upon notification in writing of an established
breach of the noise limits detailed in Planning Condition 8 the
wind turbine generator operator shall within 28 days propose a
scheme to the Local Planning Authority to mitigate the breach and
to prevent its future occurrence. This scheme shall specify the
timescales for implementation.

 
Reason: In
order to safeguard the amenities of adjoining residential occupiers
in accordance with Policy DS4 of the Copeland Local Plan
2021-2039.
 
Shadow Flicker
Protocol
 

No building or use hereby permitted
shall be occupied or use commenced until a protocol for the
management of shadow flicker on sensitive receptors has been
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority.

 
Reason: In
order to safeguard the amenities of adjoining residential occupiers
in accordance with Policy DS4 of the Copeland Local Plan
2021-2039.
 
Aviation Safety
 

Prior to commencing construction of
any wind turbine generators, or deploying any construction
equipment or temporal structure(s) 50 metres or more in height
(above ground level) the undertaker must submit an aviation
lighting scheme for the approval of the Cumberland Council in
conjunction with the Ministry of Defence defining how the
development will be lit throughout its life to maintain civil and
military aviation safety requirements as determined necessary for
aviation safety by the Ministry of Defence.

This should set
out:
a) details of any
construction equipment and temporal structures with a total height
of 50 metres or greater (above ground level) that will be deployed
during the construction of wind turbine generators and details of
any aviation warning lighting that they will be fitted with;
and
b) the locations
and heights of all wind turbine generators and any anemometry mast
featured in the development identifying those that will be fitted
with aviation warning lighting identifying the position of the
lights on the wind turbine generators; the type(s) of lights that
will be fitted and the performance specification(s) of the lighting
type(s) to be used.
Thereafter, the
undertaker must exhibit such lights as detailed in the approved
aviation lighting scheme. The lighting installed will remain
operational for the lifetime of the development.
           
Reason: To
maintain aviation safety.
 

The undertaker must notify the
Ministry of Defence, at least 14 days prior to

the commencement of
the works, in writing of the following information:
a) the date of the
commencement of the erection of wind turbine generators;
b) the maximum
height of any construction equipment to be used in the erection of
the wind turbines;
c) the date any
wind turbine generators are brought into use;
d) the latitude and
longitude and maximum heights of each wind turbine generator, and
any anemometer mast(s). The Ministry of Defence must be notified of
any changes to the information supplied in accordance with these
requirements and of the completion of the construction of the
development.
 
Reason: To
maintain aviation safety.
 

Construction/Decommissioning Management
 

Construction/decommissioning
activities that are audible at the red line boundary detailed on
Site Plan, drawing number 3369-090-SP-002 shall be carried out only
between the following hours: Monday to Friday 08.00 – 18.00
and Saturday 08.00 – 13.00 and at no time on Sunday or Public
Holidays.

Deliveries to and
removal of plant, equipment, machinery and waste from the site
shall only take place within the permitted hours.
 
Reason: In
the interests of the amenities of surrounding occupiers during the
construction and decommissioning of the development in accordance
with Policy DS4 of the Copeland Local Plan 2021-2039.
 

No development shall commence until
a Construction Traffic Management Plan (CTMP) has been submitted to
and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

The CTMP shall
include details of:
•
pre-construction road condition established by a detailed survey
for accommodation works within the highways boundary conducted with
a Highway Authority representative; with all post repairs carried
out to the satisfaction of the Local Highway Authority at the
applicants expense;
• details of
proposed crossings of the highway verge;
• retained
areas for vehicle parking, manoeuvring, loading and unloading for
their specific purpose during the development;
• cleaning of
site entrances and the adjacent public highway;
• details of
proposed wheel washing facilities;
• the sheeting
of all HGVs taking spoil to/from the site to prevent spillage or
deposit of any materials on the highway;
• construction
vehicle routing;
• the
management of junctions to and crossings of the public highway and
other public rights of way/footway;
• details of
any proposed temporary access points (vehicular / pedestrian)
• surface
water management details during the construction phase
The development
hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the
approved CTMP.
 
Reason: To
ensure the undertaking of the development does not adversely impact
upon the fabric or operation of the local highway network and in
the interests of highway and pedestrian safety in accordance with
the provisions of Policy CO4 of the Copeland Local Plan
2021-2039.
 

No development shall take place
until a site-specific Construction Environmental Management Plan
(CEMP) been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority. The plan must demonstrate the adoption and use
of the best practicable means to reduce the effects of noise,
vibration, dust and effects on the local ecological environment
during the demolition and construction phase of the works.

The development
hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the
approved CEMP.
 
Reason: To
protect amenity and to protect the environment from pollution in
accordance with Policy DS9 of the Copeland Local Plan
2021-2039.
 
Ecology
 

The development shall implement all
of the recommendations and mitigation measures contained in
Highfield Farm Wind Turbine Repowering on behalf of Axis PED
Preliminary Ecological Appraisal – Report Ref.
AxisL-043-8710.

The development
shall be carried out in accordance with the approved document
thereafter.
 
Reason: To
protect the ecological interests of the site and surrounding area
in accordance with Policy N1 of the Copeland Local Plan
2021-2039.
 
Ground
Conditions
 

In the event that contamination is
found at any time when carrying out the approved development that
was not previously identified it must be reported in writing within
14 days to the Local Planning Authority and once the Local Planning
Authority has identified the part of the site affected by the
unexpected contamination, development must be halted on that part
of the site.

An assessment must
be undertaken and where remediation is necessary a remediation
scheme, together with a timetable for its implementation, must be
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority.
The measures in the
approved remediation scheme must then be implemented in accordance
with the approved timetable. Following completion of measures
identified in the approved remediation scheme a validation report
must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority.
 
Reason: To
prevent harm to human health and the environment in accordance with
the provisions of Policy DS8 of the Copeland Local Plan
2021-2039.
 
Land Restoration
 

Within six months of the cessation
of electricity generation from the approved turbine or the expiry
of this planning permission, whichever is the sooner, all
development shall be removed from the site and the land restored in
accordance with a Land Restoration Scheme that has first been
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The Land Restoration Scheme shall relate to all
land on which both the existing and approved wind turbine
generators, and all associated infrastructure, are sited.
  

 
The Land
Restoration Scheme shall relate to all land on which the existing
wind turbine generator and approved wind turbine generator is sited
and all associated infrastructure.
The Land
Restoration Scheme shall include the following:
- An updated
Ecological Survey effort to inform the Land Restoration Scheme;
- A proposed scheme
of works for the restoration of the land including plans and
detailed specifications of the required works;
- A Construction
and Environmental Management Plan to manage the impacts of the
decommissioning and land restoration; and,
- A Construction
Traffic Management Plan to manage the impacts of the
decommissioning and land restoration.
 
Reason: For
the avoidance of doubt and to prevent harm to protected and
priority species and habitats in accordance with the provisions of
Policy N1 and Policy Ds4 of the Copeland Local Plan 2021-2039.

(Key Decision)
 
Portfolio: Sustainable, Resilient and
Connected Places
 
Relevant Scrutiny: Place Overview and
Scrutiny Committee
 
Subject:
 
The Sustainable, Resilient and Connected
Places Portfolio Holder reported that permission to procure The
Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (LEVI) concession contract
had been granted by Executive on the 8th of April 2025. 
 
Since April the Electric Vehicle team had
worked closely with internal and external colleagues and Energy
Savings trust to refine and strengthen the tender documents through
their guidance and best practice based in lessons learned from
other local authority tenders.
 
The Sustainable, Resilient and Connected
Places Portfolio Holder explained that the proposed changes were
detailed within the report and required further agreement from the
Executive.
 
Further to the Executive’s resolution on
08 April 2025, to authorise the procurement of a concession
contract for the provision, operation and maintenance of Electric
Vehicle Charging Infrastructure for public use across Cumberland
for a period of 15 years with an estimated total value of
approximately £7 Million the Sustainable, Resilient and
Connected Places Portfolio Holder moved the recommendations and the
Leader seconded them.
 
Alternative Options: Revert to the
initial Invitation to Tender (ITT)
 
DECISION:
 
That the Executive:
 
(1)      Approved the proposed amendments
to the Contract terms and Invitation To
Tender as detailed in section 2 of the LEVI (Local Electric Vehicle
Infrastructure) Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Contract
– Amendments report.
 
(2) Delegated authority to the Assistant
Director of Highways and Transport to:
(i) determine how
the bidders’ Economic Financial Standing would be assessed;
and
(ii) award the
resulting contract to the successful contractor
(Concessionaire).
 
Reasons for
Decision:
 
Given that it was a rapidly evolving area, the
updated advice provided by EST was welcomed to help ensure that the
Council’s procurement documentation was as robust and aligned
with national best practice as possible.
